errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the term of index n plus one on its own before forming the ratio; a correct written term followed by the same faulty ratio points to an algebra slip, while a faulty written term points to the substitution itself.
errors.name: Index substitution incomplete in the ratio of consecutive terms
non_conceptual_causes: an exponent of two n plus two written where two n plus three is required
the factorial incremented while the power was left unchanged
the ratio formed in one line with the term of index n plus one never written on its own
errors.observed_behavior: The response replaces n by n plus one in some places and not others, for example writing an exponent of two n plus two where two n plus three is required.
errors.scoring_consequence: A substitution error of this kind keeps the early points but blocks the final interval point (sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10014 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are algebra slips inside the substitution.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the two inequalities that the absolute value statement stands for.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped when the ratio inequality is solved
non_conceptual_causes: algebra slip
time pressure
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response converts the inequality on the ratio into a one sided inequality, producing a half interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: An inequality in absolute value alone is not sufficient for the interior point; the compound inequality is required (sg-22:21, sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the series becomes at each end of the interval; a student who says the ratio test already settled the ends holds the belief, while one who writes both endpoint series unprompted stopped early.
errors.name: Endpoints of the interval left untested
non_conceptual_causes: the ratio test finished and the part left when time ran short
the endpoints named and the two series never written out
the open interval copied from the inequality straight to the answer line
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the open interval found from the ratio test as the interval of convergence without examining either endpoint.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the endpoint consideration point and the interval point are lost (sg-25:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the first three terms at that endpoint before naming a test; a student who then keeps the same test holds the belief, while one who switches tests had not produced the terms.
errors.name: Endpoint series analysed with a test whose conditions it fails
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoint series never written out before a test was named
the alternating factor lost when a negative endpoint was substituted
the test reused from the other endpoint with no recheck of its conditions
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies a comparison test to an alternating series, or applies the alternating series test to a series of positive terms.
errors.scoring_consequence: The analysis point at that endpoint is lost, and the interval point with it (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to list the conditions the named test requires; a student who cannot produce them holds the belief, while one who recites them and points to scratch work omitted them in presentation only.
errors.name: Test named without its hypotheses being checked
non_conceptual_causes: the test named on the last line with the conditions left in scratch work
the conditions assumed to carry over from the series in the previous part
the name of the test written in place of the argument because the part ran long
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99008.
errors.observed_behavior: The response names a convergence test and states a conclusion without establishing the conditions the test requires.
errors.scoring_consequence: Points tied to the conditions or to the justification are lost even when the verdict is right (sg-21:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which terms the partial sum contains and which term comes next; a student who names the next term correctly and still bounds with another term has a counting slip, while one who cannot say which term is omitted is applying the bound without its conditions.
errors.name: Bounding term taken from the wrong position in the series
non_conceptual_causes: the last index of the partial sum counted as the first omitted index
the sum read as ending at n when the sigma runs to n minus one
the bounding term taken from the term that was easiest to evaluate
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response bounds the error with a term already included in the partial sum, or with a term further along than the first omitted one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point is earned only for the correct omitted term, and a term of higher degree does not earn it (sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10017 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are counting slips in locating the first omitted term.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what value of the variable the approximation is being made at; a student who names it and still substitutes the index is not separating index from variable, while one who recomputes on the spot made a substitution slip.
errors.name: Bounding term evaluated at the wrong input
non_conceptual_causes: the index n substituted in place of the stated input
the centre of the series substituted because the term was read from the general form
a power of a negative input evaluated without parentheses
errors.observed_behavior: The response identifies the correct omitted term but substitutes the index, the centre, or another value in place of the stated input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point attached to using the term correctly is lost (sg-22:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the error is known exactly or only bounded and which symbol says so; a student who claims exact knowledge holds the belief, while one who names the inequality wrote the relation loosely.
errors.name: Error written as equal to the bounding term
non_conceptual_causes: the equals sign used to join the error and the bound as one line of work
the inequality symbol chosen after the value was computed and pointed the wrong way
the phrase at most in the prompt not carried into the written relation
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016, BC-ERR-99002.
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the error as equal to the bounding expression rather than at most that expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: A statement of equality does not earn the justification point in either bound (sg-22:21, sg-23:20, sg-24:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to finish the sentence stating what the error is less than; a student who supplies the tolerance at once omitted a line, while one who offers the bound as the answer is treating bound and error as one object.
errors.name: Comparison with the tolerance left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: the bounding value computed and the comparison sentence left unwritten
the tolerance read as the number to compute rather than the number to beat
the comparison carried out mentally with only the verdict recorded
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the bounding value but never states that it is at most the tolerance the prompt named.
errors.scoring_consequence: The communication point requires the inequality against the tolerance to be presented (sg-23:20, sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-99007 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are omissions in presenting the final comparison.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the series alternates, whether a derivative bound is supplied, and whether the error is known or bounded; the first two answers separate the choice of bound from the belief that the bound is the error.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Some responses did not state the conditions for applying the alternating series error bound, and some reached for the Lagrange bound instead.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Responses failed to tie the bound to the absolute difference between approximation and exact value, or did not show the bound was less than the target.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: A significant number did not observe that the series alternates, some used the Lagrange bound, and some treated the series as geometric.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Responses wrote the error equal to 0.01 or strictly less than 0.01; the report states the error is not equal to and the bound is not strictly less than that value.

errors.name: Error bound conditions not stated, or error confused with error bound
non_conceptual_causes: the bound recalled as a formula with its conditions left unwritten
the inequality symbol chosen after the value was computed
the two bounds not separated because only one had been used in recent practice
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses invoke an error bound without confirming that the series alternates with terms decreasing to zero, reach for the Lagrange bound where the alternating series bound applies, or write the error as equal to or strictly less than the bound instead of at most the bound.
errors.scoring_consequence: The condition or analysis point is lost even when the numerical bound is computed correctly.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise comparing and contrasting the alternating series error bound with the Lagrange error bound, and giving repeated practice in communicating the difference between an error and an error bound.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to substitute n equal to one and two into the proposed general term.
errors.name: General term of a series mis-differentiated or mis-assembled
non_conceptual_causes: algebra slip in the exponent
off by one slip in the index
time pressure
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99018.
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes several correct terms but produces a general term that does not reproduce them, often after differentiating with respect to the index or mishandling the alternating factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The general term is a separate scored point from the first terms (sg-25:26, sg-24:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what degree the requested polynomial has and which terms belong to it; a student who says the polynomial and the series are the same object holds the belief, while one who names the degree and strikes the extra terms copied from a neighbouring part.
errors.name: Polynomial presented with extra terms or a trailing ellipsis
non_conceptual_causes: the ellipsis carried over from a series written in an earlier part
the requested degree read as a number of terms
extra terms retained because the expansion was produced before the degree was checked
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes a polynomial that includes terms beyond the requested degree, or appends an ellipsis, turning the answer into a series.
errors.scoring_consequence: A polynomial with terms of higher degree, or with an ellipsis, does not earn the final polynomial point (sg-23:20, sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which letter is being differentiated with respect to and ask for the derivative of the general term alone; a derivative taken with respect to the index identifies the object confusion, while a correct derivative with a wrong coefficient identifies the arithmetic.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Many responses could not compute the derivative with respect to x of the given general term.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Responses omitted the chain rule or made product rule errors when finding the fourth derivative used to build the Taylor polynomial.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Some differentiated with respect to n, some used the quotient rule, and some integrated the series instead.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Simplification errors in the coefficient of the third term were the most common reason the first terms point was not earned, and parentheses were omitted in the general term.

errors.name: General term of a power series mis-differentiated or mis-assembled
non_conceptual_causes: the index and the variable not distinguished inside the general term
the coefficient arithmetic carried out in a single step
the pattern inferred from displayed terms that were themselves wrong
errors.observed_behavior: Responses can write the first several terms of a series but cannot differentiate the general term, apply the quotient rule to it, differentiate with respect to the index, or simplify the resulting coefficient correctly.
errors.scoring_consequence: The general term point is not earned; the first terms point may be earned separately.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise practising Taylor polynomials for composite and product functions, and building the general term of a differentiated series from a correctly written general term rather than from a guessed pattern.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the student entered into the calculator, written as an integral.
errors.name: Calculator answer presented with no setup
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a belief that the work is scratch
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears with no integral and no evidence of the division.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost; an unsupported value can still earn an answer point only where the guideline says so (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to report the same value to six digits; a student who can produce them rounded on presentation, while one who cannot recover them used a trace or reused a rounded intermediate.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Some responses rounded the average value to a whole number.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Some responses used the trace function and found a solution not correct to three digits after the decimal.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Responses reporting t equals 3.14 or 3 did not earn the point because these are not correct to three digits after the decimal.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Some responses presented fewer than three correct digits, and those that did tended to do so throughout the question.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: A presented answer of 5.1 or 5.13 did not earn the answer point because of the decimal presentation error.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Responses that earned the product point usually lost the answer point only through decimal presentation errors.

errors.name: Decimal presentation error or premature rounding
non_conceptual_causes: the intermediate value not stored and the rounded figure reused
a trace used where a solver was needed
the answer copied at the precision shown on the calculator screen
errors.observed_behavior: Responses report fewer than three digits after the decimal point, round an intermediate value before it is used again, or read a value off a trace rather than solving for it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned; the report notes this recurs across several parts of the same response.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise storing intermediate values in the calculator, presenting answers correct to three places after the decimal throughout the year, and solving equations with a solver rather than a trace.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same function on an interval of length one and then on an interval of length four and ask for both averages.
errors.name: Average value reported without dividing by the interval length
non_conceptual_causes: the divisor was written in the setup and dropped when the value was transcribed
the interval length was computed as the sum of the endpoints rather than their difference
the response stopped after the integral was evaluated when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the correct definite integral and reports its value as the average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The average value point is lost unless the correct answer appears elsewhere as evidence of the division (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of the reported answer; rate units name an average value and accumulated units name a total.
errors.name: Integral reported without the division in an average value
non_conceptual_causes: computed the integral on the calculator and reported the display without the division
took the interval length to be one from a previous part where it was
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral is presented as the average value with no division by the length of the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The average value formula point is lost; a correct integral together with the correct quotient value earns both points even when the linkage is unclear (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to list every candidate input before justifying.
errors.name: Local argument offered where a global extremum is requested
non_conceptual_causes: habit carried over from relative extremum questions
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification for an absolute extreme value on a closed interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is not earned, although the answer point remains available with the correct value (sg-25:19, sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the value at the endpoint has been compared with the value at the critical point.
errors.name: Local argument offered for an absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that an accumulated amount is largest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value at each endpoint and at every interior critical point; a student who supplies them and then names the largest was missing the arithmetic, while one who says the sign change already settles it holds the local-for-global belief.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Many responses did not evaluate N at both endpoints and the interior critical point, justifying only a local maximum.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Responses gave only a sign change of g prime at x equals 5 without stating it is the only critical point on the interval.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Very rarely did responses consider all three critical points, and some reported only a local minimum without the endpoints.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Justifications other than the candidates test presented local arguments that did not explain the behaviour of A over the whole interval.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Incomplete candidates tests left out x equals 6 or x equals 12 without arguing why those cannot be the minimum.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Local arguments and candidates tests containing errors were the common reasons the justification point was not earned.

errors.name: Local argument offered where a global argument is required
non_conceptual_causes: the candidates listed and the endpoint values never computed from the given representation
a sign chart drawn and never translated into a sentence about the whole interval
the argument copied from a relative extremum part earlier in the same question
errors.observed_behavior: Responses justify an absolute maximum or minimum on a closed interval by a sign change at one point, or run an incomplete candidates test that omits an endpoint or an interior critical point.
errors.official_evidence_notes: 2023 AB/BC Q4(d), cr-23:16; 2025 AB/BC Q1(D), crabbc-25:4; 2025 AB/BC Q4(D), crabbc-25:18
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point for the absolute extremum is not earned; the answer point may still be available.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise practising both forms of argument, the candidates test and a full interval sign argument, and having students identify which situations call for each.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative decides whether a rate is increasing; a student who names the first derivative is answering about the quantity, while one who names the second and still cites both signs combined them without cause.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Many responses answered that the temperature was decreasing because the first derivative was negative, which was true but did not answer whether the rate of change was increasing or decreasing; the report states the correct argument uses the positive second derivative on the interval.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Responses argued the particle was moving toward the x-axis from the sign of dy/dx or said only that y is decreasing rather than that the derivative is negative.

errors.name: Direction of change confused with the sign of the quantity itself
non_conceptual_causes: the words increasing and decreasing attached to the quantity rather than to its rate
both derivative signs available and combined without a reason for doing so
the question read as asking whether the quantity itself is increasing
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses answer a question about whether a quantity is changing at an increasing or decreasing rate by appealing to the sign of the first derivative, or by pointing to the opposing signs of the first and second derivatives, rather than to the sign of the second derivative alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reasoning point is not earned even when the stated conclusion is correct.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise precise language separating a quantity, its rate of change and the rate at which that rate changes, and requiring the reasoning to name which derivative is being used.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity was larger or smaller a moment later: an answer that the sign carries no information is consistent with BC-MIS-04002, an answer drawn from the amount rather than its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and a correct direction beside the unsigned written answer is consistent with the transcription and template causes.
errors.name: Sign of a rate not interpreted
non_conceptual_causes: the minus sign is dropped when the value is copied from the calculator
the stem's word decreasing is read as an instruction to report a magnitude
the interpretation sentence is written from the previous part's template
errors.observed_behavior: A negative rate is reported as a magnitude or is described as an increase.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records the same confusion of direction with quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite the sentence with every pronoun replaced by a name: restating the conclusion as the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, treating the presence of symbols as completing the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the object correctly at once is consistent with the carry-over and timing causes.
errors.name: Justification uses an unnamed referent
non_conceptual_causes: the pronoun is carried over from the stem's own wording
the sentence is written at speed at the end of the part
the object is named once in an earlier part and treated as still named
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the function or the graph changes sign, without naming which object is meant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the 2025 guideline names an ambiguous referent as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a circular sector of stated radius and angle.
errors.name: Factor of one half omitted from a polar area integral
non_conceptual_causes: the factor was written outside the integral in scratch work and not carried forward
the constant was left for a final multiplication that was never applied
errors.observed_behavior: The area integrand is the square of r with no factor of one half.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is twice the area, so the answer point is lost; the factor is assessed with the limits (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a full circle from the polar formula and compare.
errors.name: Polar area integrand written without squaring r
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the integrand was keyed in
the setup was copied from an arc length exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is of r with respect to theta rather than of the square of r.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point, which requires an integral containing the square of r, is lost (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the written expression aloud as a sentence; a student who reads a constant of integration on a definite integral has not separated the two notations, while one who reads the limits back in the wrong order took them from the wrong pair.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Responses wrote the rate function equal to its own definite integral, placed a summation sign before the integral, or appended a constant of integration to a definite integral; some reversed the limits or used limits of 6 and 10.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: The report notes that most responses displayed the required definite integral correctly, so these notational statements were the minority pattern.

errors.name: Definite integral expression written in malformed notation
non_conceptual_causes: the notation assembled from remembered fragments under time pressure
indefinite and definite integral notation not separated, so a constant of integration was attached
the limits taken from the wrong pair of values in the stem
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses asked for an integral expression write statements that are not integral expressions, such as the function set equal to its own integral, a summation sign placed in front of an integral, or a constant of integration attached to a definite integral, and some reverse the limits or use limits that were never given.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression point is not earned, since the requested object is an integral expression and nothing else is being scored in that part.
errors.teacher_advice: The report advises practising notational fluency by presenting the same communicated mathematics in several equivalent representations (cr-22:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which angles the two curves meet.
errors.name: Polar limits taken from the wrong angles
non_conceptual_causes: the angle interval was taken from the axes of the figure rather than from the intersection angles
one intersection angle was solved for and the other was copied from the stem
errors.observed_behavior: The area integral runs over the angle interval of the figure rather than between the intersection angles of the two curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, since the limits are assessed there (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to describe in words what happens to each part of the expression as the input grows, with no symbol substituted.
errors.name: Infinity substituted as a number
non_conceptual_causes: the substitution habit from a finite limit is carried into the end behaviour computation
the infinity symbol is written into the expression on the scratch line and then treated as a coefficient
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the infinity symbol into the expression and performs arithmetic with it.
errors.scoring_consequence: Arithmetic performed with the infinity symbol is treated as scratch work and does not earn the value point (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical length or volume reported with no integral shown
non_conceptual_causes: the expression was kept on the calculator screen and never transcribed
the answer line was written last with the setup left in scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for an arc length or a volume with no integral expression anywhere in the response.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of the semicircular piece alone before the integral is assembled.
errors.name: Semicircular region given the area of a full circle
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the circle area formula from memory and never halved it
read the radius off the figure as the diameter
halved the area in the working and copied the unhalved line into the integral
errors.observed_behavior: The area of a semicircular piece of the region is computed as pi times the radius squared.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point for that integral is lost.
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the rest of the region is handled correctly and the departure is confined to the recalled area formula.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the integral before any number is computed.
errors.name: Regions below the axis added as positive area
non_conceptual_causes: added the pieces on the calculator as magnitudes and never reinstated the sign
read the region below the axis as above it because the figure is shaded on both sides
errors.observed_behavior: Every piece of the region is added with a positive sign, so a signed integral is reported as a plain area.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost, and any later part that imports the value inherits the error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the unsimplified expression would answer the question; a student who says it would and simplified anyway is following a habit, and comparing the two forms locates the arithmetic step that introduced the error.

errors.name: Unnecessary simplification introducing arithmetic or algebra errors
non_conceptual_causes: a classroom habit of simplifying every expression before reporting it
fraction arithmetic carried out mentally during the simplification
a tangent line equation solved for y where point-slope form would have been accepted

errors.observed_behavior: Responses simplify a numerical or algebraic expression that the exam does not require to be simplified, and introduce sign, order of operations or fraction errors that spoil an otherwise correct result.
errors.scoring_consequence: A point already secured by the correct setup can be lost when the simplified final form is wrong.
errors.single_cause_note: No BC-MIS record corresponds to this behaviour; it is a working habit rather than a belief about calculus, so the alternatives below are all non-conceptual.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise reminding students that the free-response section does not require simplification, while still practising the underlying arithmetic and algebra.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integral from a to x of f prime equals in terms of f at both ends; a student who omits the value at the lower limit holds the belief, while one who writes both terms and still reports the wrong sign mishandled the reversed limits.

errors.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus misapplied to an accumulation function
non_conceptual_causes: the lower limit of integration assumed to be zero
a reversal of the limits not recognised as a change of sign
the initial condition stated in the stem never carried into the calculation
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses write the integral of f prime from a to x as f of x, ignoring the value at the lower limit, or mishandle a reversed pair of limits and report the wrong sign for an accumulated area.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value or setup point in that part is not earned, and the error usually propagates to later parts that build on the value.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise varying the lower limit of integration in practice problems, including cases where the lower limit exceeds the upper limit, and contrasting the several similar looking expressions built from f, f prime and an integral sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the proposed answer and compare it with the integrand.
errors.name: Factors of a product antidifferentiated separately
non_conceptual_causes: carried the term by term habit over from the sum rule practised immediately before
began parts on scratch paper and copied the first line of the wrong attempt
errors.observed_behavior: The response antidifferentiates each factor of a product and multiplies the results.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the u and dv point nor the expression point is earned (sg-23:18, sg-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the last computed line and the reported answer side by side; a student who defends the sign change on the grounds that the quantity cannot be negative holds the area belief, while one who spots the conflict never checked.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Some responses concluded that the value of the Riemann sum must be positive and reported 51 in spite of having correctly calculated negative 51.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Responses carried an incorrect value from part (a) into the candidates test and did not recognise that it contradicted their own correct conclusion in part (c) that the function was decreasing on that interval.

errors.name: Reported answer contradicts the response's own work
non_conceptual_causes: the final value written from an expectation of the form the answer should take
an earlier incorrect value carried forward without being compared with a later conclusion
no check of the reported answer against the work directly above it
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses compute a correct intermediate result and then report a final value inconsistent with it, such as changing the sign of a negative sum or carrying forward an earlier incorrect value that contradicts a later correct conclusion, without noticing the conflict.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the supporting work would have earned it, and in the extremum case the justification point is lost as well.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-08024 is a plausible internal cause, and it covers the sign case alone; the remaining routes are failures to check the answer against the work.
errors.teacher_advice: The report advises that when work does not lead to the stated result students should backtrack to find where the error originated rather than adjust the answer, and that every step must be consistent (cr-23:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the complete candidate list on its own, before any values are compared.
errors.name: Candidates comparison left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: found the critical inputs and listed only those, leaving the endpoints on scratch paper
miscounted the sign changes and stopped the table one row early
errors.observed_behavior: A candidates table omits an endpoint or a critical input, or includes an input that is neither.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point requires evaluations or reasoning at every critical input and both endpoints and no others (sg-25:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the function value at the input and for the value approached, as two separate questions, and see whether the student gives two different numbers.
errors.name: Function value reported as the limit
non_conceptual_causes: the open circle and the filled point are close together on the figure and the filled one is read
the row of the table at the target input is copied instead of the rows around it
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives the plotted or defined value of the function at the input in place of the value the function approaches there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reading point is lost, and in a continuity part the comparison of limit with value collapses.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw the configuration and label every length before writing a formula: an answer assembled from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that differentiates against a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a correct formula once the diagram is drawn is consistent with the recall and shape causes.
errors.name: Relating equation wrong or absent
non_conceptual_causes: the geometric formula is misremembered, for instance a cone's volume without the factor one third
no diagram is drawn so the configuration is guessed
the formula is taken from a similar problem with a different shape
errors.observed_behavior: No equation ties the quantities together, or the formula used does not describe the configuration.
errors.scoring_consequence: Nothing downstream can be earned; BC-ERR-99011 records integrands chosen from the wrong area or volume family as the analogous failure in Unit 8.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what variable the requested rate is taken with respect to, before differentiating: an answer naming a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, an answer that the two derivative variables give the same object is consistent with BC-MIS-99005, and naming time correctly beside the wrong written derivative is consistent with the ordering and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation carried out with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: the differentiation is carried out against the variable that appears first
the chain rule factor with respect to time is written and not carried to the next line
the habit of differentiating with respect to x is carried from the implicit differentiation topic
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation is differentiated with respect to a length or with respect to x, and the response stops there rather than continuing through the chain rule to a rate with respect to time.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader report for 2024 records that responses differentiating with respect to x needed to continue through the chain rule and that many provided no work beyond that step (cr-24:18); BC-ERR-99013 records the same family across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity is divided by what to produce the reported number; a student who builds the ratio correctly and still gives the original units treated units as a label, while one who cannot name the two quantities has the units gap in the derivation.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Responses reported centimetres squared per day or centimetres per day, or no units, for a second derivative approximation.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Several responses gave no acceleration units or gave meters per second.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Most recognised the units would be a ratio but made errors in the numerator, the denominator or both.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Many responses gave units for the rate rather than for its derivative, or gave none at all.

errors.name: Units omitted or built incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the numerator or the denominator of the ratio misidentified when the units were assembled
the units written from the quantity in the stem rather than from the derived quantity
the explicit request for units read past in the prompt
errors.observed_behavior: Responses give no units where units are requested, or report units of the original quantity instead of the derived one, for example words per minute for a second difference quotient.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is not earned; it is scored separately from the value.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise dimensional analysis practice, and a habit of circling the units given in a table or on the axes and then dividing or multiplying them according to whether a derivative or an antiderivative is being taken.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same derivative with an inner function whose derivative is neither one nor a constant, and ask the student to point at the factor that came from inside.
errors.name: Inner derivative omitted from a chain rule application
non_conceptual_causes: the inner function is linear, so the missing factor changes only a coefficient and passes unnoticed
the inner derivative is computed on scratch work and never carried into the product
the response stops at the first line after the setup, leaving the second factor unwritten
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the outer function correctly and stops, leaving the derivative of the inner function out of the product.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong, and in a multipart question the error propagates into every later part that uses it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the given equation supplies at the stated point; a student who says it must be solved first holds the belief that the equation is an equation for the quantity, while one who evaluates it on request took a longer route by habit.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Several responses computed a second derivative to find the slope of the tangent line, and others held that the equation had to be solved by separation of variables first.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Some responses attempted to solve the differential equation for the function in the tangent line part, which the report calls a significant misconception about a first-order differential equation.

errors.name: Differential equation solved where it already supplies the slope
non_conceptual_causes: the phrase differential equation read as an instruction to solve
the tangent line procedure recalled as requiring an explicit formula for the function
time spent on an unnecessary general solution before the requested step
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses asked for a tangent line or an approximation from a given differential equation first attempt to find the general solution by separation of variables, or compute a second derivative, instead of evaluating the given equation at the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is at risk and the part is often left incomplete, since the unnecessary work consumes the part without producing the requested value.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise building the connection between a contextual rate and the slope of a tangent line, and reminding students that the given equation supplies the slope directly (cr-23:13).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which terms belong on which side before any integral is written.
errors.name: Variables not separated before antidifferentiating
non_conceptual_causes: began antidifferentiating as soon as an integral sign was written
separated the variables on scratch paper and integrated the original line on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: The response antidifferentiates the equation as written, with both variables on the same side.
errors.scoring_consequence: All four points of the separation part are lost; the guideline states that a response with no separation earns none of them.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the answer would be if the starting value were different; a family produced on request points away from BC-MIS-07016.
errors.name: Constant of integration omitted
non_conceptual_causes: carried the habit over from the definite integrals worked immediately before
wrote the constant on the first line and lost it when the exponential was taken
errors.observed_behavior: The antiderivative equation is written with no constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: At most the first two points are available; the guideline caps the response there.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which equation the initial values were substituted into and what the constant stands for there.
errors.name: Constant evaluated after the exponentiation instead of before
non_conceptual_causes: substituted the initial values into whichever line was nearest on the page
exponentiated first out of habit and did not revisit the constant
errors.observed_behavior: The response exponentiates first and then substitutes the initial condition into an expression where the constant has changed form.
errors.scoring_consequence: The constant point is at risk; the guideline earns it for including the constant in an equation and substituting the initial values into it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the reported solution and compare it with the original equation; a mismatch traced to one antiderivative is a technique gap, while a separation that leaves both variables on one side points to the belief that any equation separates.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Many responses could not antidifferentiate the sine term or the reciprocal term, and algebra errors were common at each step.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Responses reported the integral of dM over 40 minus M as a positive logarithm, and simplified exponentials incorrectly.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Separations were spoiled by the position of the constant, the cosine antiderivative was wrong in several forms, and some substituted t equals 4 with H equals 0.

errors.name: Separable differential equation separated or antidifferentiated incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: a constant factor left on the side carrying the wrong differential
the substitution the antiderivative required never selected
the initial condition applied after the algebra rather than where the constant first appears
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses leave a variable on the wrong side of the separation, misplace a constant factor, produce an incorrect antiderivative of a trigonometric or reciprocal term, or mishandle the sign and the absolute value in a logarithm before solving for the dependent variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The separation, antiderivative and constant points are assessed separately, so an early slip costs several points in the part.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise classifying worked separations as correctly separated, poorly separated or not separated, and applying the initial condition as soon as the constant of integration first appears.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the units or the degree of the reported derivative are, and compare them with the degree the quotient should give.
errors.name: Denominator square omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the square is written on scratch work and is lost in the transcription
the denominator is long, so it is copied once without its exponent
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the quotient rule with the denominator rather than its square below the line.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input: keeping it as a critical point regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, treating the domain gap as not interrupting the behaviour is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, and dropping it once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and calculator causes.
errors.name: Solutions outside the domain retained as critical points
non_conceptual_causes: a factor is cancelled from the derivative although it also vanishes in the denominator
the domain of the original function is never written down
the root comes from a calculator zero with no check that the function has a value there
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input at which the derivative expression vanishes although the function itself is undefined there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The candidate list is wrong and the comparison that follows cannot be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether more than one function has the given derivative.
errors.name: Constant of integration omitted from an indefinite integral
non_conceptual_causes: omission under time pressure
habit carried over from definite integrals
errors.observed_behavior: An indefinite integral is reported without an arbitrary constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point for an indefinite integral is lost when the constant is required by the stem.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to compare the two degrees before any decomposition is written.
errors.name: Improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division
non_conceptual_causes: began decomposing as soon as the denominator factored, without comparing degrees
read the numerator degree off the leading term of an unexpanded product
errors.observed_behavior: A rational integrand whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree is split into partial fractions directly.
errors.scoring_consequence: The decomposition cannot be solved consistently and the antiderivative point is not earned.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the integrand is continuous before the integral is set up.
errors.name: Integral split at a discontinuity omitted
non_conceptual_causes: read only the first branch of the piecewise definition
noticed the jump and split the interval on scratch paper but antidifferentiated the single expression on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: A function with a jump on the interval of integration is antidifferentiated as a single expression across the jump.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost because the antiderivative used is not valid across the whole interval.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what number the infinity symbol stands for in that substitution; a student who supplies a value treats it as a number, while one who rewrites with a bound b and a limit had dropped notation.
errors.name: Improper integral evaluated without limit notation
non_conceptual_causes: the infinity symbol substituted directly into the antiderivative
limit notation opened on the first line and dropped at the evaluation line
the letter used as the upper bound changed between the integral and the limit
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99007.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the infinity symbol into the antiderivative, or opens with limit notation and abandons it before the evaluation is finished.
errors.scoring_consequence: The evaluation point requires correct limit notation; an evaluation written with the infinity symbol does not earn it (sg-21:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a convergent and a divergent integral from the same family and ask which converges and why.
errors.name: Value reported for a divergent improper integral
non_conceptual_causes: substituted the infinite limit directly into the antiderivative instead of taking a limit
evaluated the limit of the wrong branch after a sign slip in the antiderivative
errors.observed_behavior: The response produces a finite number although the limit is infinite or fails to exist.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is not earned because the required conclusion is a statement of divergence.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the coefficient of the second degree term is when the second derivative at the centre is six; an answer of six points to the belief, while an answer of three followed by later omissions points to an inconsistent application.
errors.name: Taylor coefficient written without dividing by the factorial
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative value written straight into the coefficient slot
the factorial placed in the numerator instead of the denominator
the factorial included for the second degree term and omitted thereafter
errors.observed_behavior: The response places the derivative value directly as the coefficient of the power, with no factorial denominator.
errors.scoring_consequence: The polynomial is not the requested one and its term points are lost (sg-23:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative belongs in the coefficient of the third degree term and why; a student who names the third derivative and still reads the wrong row made a table slip, while one who names a different order is not tying order to degree.
errors.name: Derivative values taken from the wrong row or order
non_conceptual_causes: a row of the table read one line off
the order of the derivative paired with the power by position in the table rather than by order
a value read from a column for a different centre
errors.observed_behavior: The response reads a table of derivative values and pairs a derivative of one order with the power of another.
errors.scoring_consequence: Each misplaced value spoils the term that depends on it.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10019 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are misreadings of the table layout.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the first three terms of the cosine series and of the exponential series separately; a student who gives the same sign pattern for both has merged two memorised lists, while one who separates them and still drops factorials has a recall gap in the coefficients.
errors.name: Standard Maclaurin series recalled incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the alternating factor of the cosine series attached to the exponential series
even powers written where odd powers belong in the sine series
the factorial denominators omitted, so the expansion reduces to a geometric form
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the series for the exponential, the sine, the cosine, or one over one minus x with wrong signs, wrong parities of the powers, or missing factorials.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every term built on the misremembered series is wrong, so the dependent points are lost (sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite the integrand with the parentheses restored and compare the two expressions; a student who sees no difference is not tracking the order of subtraction, while one who spots the missing distribution made a copying slip.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Responses failed to distribute the negative one across the parentheses when writing f of x minus g of x, and repeated the error in the squared integrand.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Responses had difficulty distributing a negative across parentheses when evaluating the antiderivative.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Correct expressions in f and g were spoiled when the given expressions were substituted without parentheses.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Missing parentheses in the integrand occurred when a response substituted the given functions rather than leaving the integrand in f and g notation.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Parentheses omitted around the product of a binomial and an exponential expression.

errors.name: Parentheses lost when a given expression is substituted into an integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the subtraction carried across the first term of the substituted expression only
the grouping parentheses lost while a long expression was copied by hand
the rewrite undertaken at all where the function names would have carried the setup
errors.observed_behavior: Responses that replace named functions by their given analytic expressions fail to distribute a subtraction or omit the grouping parentheses, changing the integrand.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point is lost; the answer point may survive if a correct calculator value is also reported.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise using the function names given in the stem rather than copying analytic expressions, and using parentheses to group an integrand and to separate it from the differential.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units alone, with no computation: units offered as optional is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, units of the quantity given for its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and correct units spoken with the written answer bare is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Units omitted or assembled the wrong way round
non_conceptual_causes: the units are written on scratch work and not transferred to the answer line
the unit of the independent variable is taken from a different sentence of the stem
the part is reached at the end of the question and the answer line is filled last
errors.observed_behavior: A correct numerical rate is reported with no units, or with the units of the quantity alone, or with the numerator and denominator units exchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is a separate point in the 2024 and 2025 table based questions and is lost outright (sg-24:2, sg-25:11); BC-ERR-99005 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different.
errors.name: Interpretation left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
the sentence is abbreviated after a long computation
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation names the quantity but omits the instant or interval, the direction of change, or the units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99027 records incomplete interpretation in context across the Chief Reader reports.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to say what the number measures, over what interval, and in what units; a student who restates the number holds the belief that a value is an interpretation, while one who supplies the parts on request abbreviated the sentence.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Many interpretations of the derivative failed to describe the value as a rate of a rate or to say that the rate was decreasing.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Responses had difficulty giving a correct interpretation containing the phrases average temperature and the interval from t equals 0 to t equals 12.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Some responses reported that the temperature was decreasing, which was true but did not answer what was asked.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Many responses identified the integral as an arc length but made no mention of the interval, and some called it a distance.

errors.name: Interpretation of a value in context left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: the interpretation written before the units had been settled
the interval named in the stem not repeated in the sentence
the word rate used once where a rate of a rate is meant
errors.observed_behavior: Responses interpret a derivative or an integral without naming the quantity, the interval, or the fact that a rate is itself changing, or they answer a different question than the one asked.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point requires the key phrases, so an answer missing the interval or the rate of a rate is not earned.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise using the language of the course framework as a template for interpretations, and drawing on published scoring guidelines to see the terminology that earns interpretation points.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that was entered, and check whether it names the function and the input.
errors.name: Calculator derivative reported without a setup
non_conceptual_causes: the calculator result is transcribed directly and the setup stays on the calculator screen
the setup line is written after the value and is not reached before the part ends
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives a numerical derivative value with no indication of what was computed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost although the value may be right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variable is being integrated over and where the expression says so; a student who says it makes no difference holds the belief, while one who supplies dt at once left it off in transcription.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Occasionally responses failed to include the differential dt in the integral for total vehicles.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Setups omitted the differential or used the wrong one, dy instead of dt.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Many responses left dt out of the setup for x of 1, giving an ambiguous expression that could not be credited.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Setups such as negative 3 plus an integral of v of t with no differential, or with dx.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Definite integrals presented without a differential, producing ambiguous setups for y of 0.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Omitting a differential could lead to mishandling the constant and to losing the integrand or antiderivative point.

errors.name: Differential omitted from an integral expression
non_conceptual_causes: the integrand copied from the stem and the expression closed without the differential
the differential written in the variable that also names a limit of integration
the differential omitted because the integral was assembled from remembered fragments
errors.observed_behavior: Responses present a definite integral with no differential, or with a differential in the wrong variable, producing a setup the reader cannot interpret.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is not earned when the resulting expression is ambiguous; in some parts later points in that part are also lost.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise insisting on the differential in every integral expression and on parentheses that separate the integrand from the differential.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the variable of integration in the expression as written.
errors.name: Differential omitted from an integral expression
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
arithmetic slip
errors.observed_behavior: An integral is written with limits and an integrand but no dx, dt, or dy.
errors.scoring_consequence: Whether the point survives depends on the guideline; in 2023 a missing differential kept the setup point but could block the answer point when the expression was also equated to a value (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the net rate should be at a time when the two rates are equal.
errors.name: Inflow and outflow rates added instead of subtracted
non_conceptual_causes: the two rate names in the stem were assigned to the wrong roles
a minus sign was dropped while the two rate expressions were combined
the second rate was copied from the wrong table column
errors.observed_behavior: The net rate is written as the sum of the two rates, or the difference is taken in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to say in one sentence what the chart shows about the interval named in the prompt: an answer that the sampled signs settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-04017, an answer that restates the chart as its own reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and a fluent sentence with none written is consistent with the timing and interval causes.
errors.name: Sign chart presented with no stated reading
non_conceptual_causes: the reading sentence is left to the end of the part and not reached
the chart is treated as sufficient because an earlier part accepted one
the chart covers an interval other than the one the prompt names
errors.observed_behavior: A number line or table of signs appears with no sentence saying what it shows about the direction of motion over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 report records that responses failing to communicate what the chart showed over the whole interval did not earn the analysis points (crabbc-25:22, crabbc-25:23); BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justification across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the amount at both ends of the interval.
errors.name: Endpoints omitted from a candidates table
non_conceptual_causes: the candidates table was started and left unfinished when time ran out
the endpoint values were computed on the calculator and never transcribed
errors.observed_behavior: The candidates test evaluates the amount only at the interior critical point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is not global (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how the candidate compares with the value at the far end of the interval.
errors.name: Local argument offered where a global argument is required
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
misread of the question or the figure
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies an absolute extremum with a first derivative test or a second derivative test at the candidate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point stays available with the correct value.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same rate with two different starting amounts and ask for the later value in each case.
errors.name: Initial value not added to the accumulated change
non_conceptual_causes: the initial amount in the stem was read as the amount at the end of the interval
the addition was done mentally and the sum was never written
the response stopped after the integral when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the integral of the rate and reports it as the value of the quantity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the region the integral just written covers.
errors.name: Symmetry used without the compensating factor
non_conceptual_causes: the doubling was done in scratch work and not carried to the answer line
the limits were halved and the factor of two was applied as well
errors.observed_behavior: Half of a symmetric region is integrated and the result is reported without doubling, or a full region is doubled as well.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported area is half or twice the correct value and the answer point is lost; the correctly doubled form earned all points in 2025 (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the origin at an angle inside the interval.
errors.name: Inner and outer polar radii exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the two radius labels were exchanged when the integrand was written
the radii were compared at an angle outside the interval
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand subtracts the square of the outer radius from the square of the inner radius.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative area is produced and the integrand point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both Cartesian coordinates of the point at a stated angle.
errors.name: Polar radius used as a Cartesian coordinate
non_conceptual_causes: the value of r returned by the calculator was written on the x line
both conversion formulas were written and only one was applied
errors.observed_behavior: The value of r is treated as the x coordinate or the y coordinate of the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The coordinate is wrong, so any extremum or conversion built on it fails.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sine of one and compare with the value the response used.
errors.name: Calculator work performed in degree mode
non_conceptual_causes: the calculator was left in degree mode from an earlier question
the mode was changed for one computation and not changed back
the values looked plausible so the mode was never checked
errors.observed_behavior: Trigonometric values throughout a question are computed in degree measure, producing internally consistent but wrong numbers.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response does not earn the first point it would otherwise have earned and is generally eligible for the rest (sg-23:6, sg-23:7).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-09008 is plausible as an internal cause, and it covers just the missing expression; the mode itself is a setting, so the non-conceptual causes carry the alternatives.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the equality by substituting the value of the parameter.
errors.name: Variable expression equated to a numerical value
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
careless transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A chain such as an expression in t set equal to its value at one time is written as a single equality.
errors.scoring_consequence: In 2023 such a response earned one of the two available points (sg-23:6); in 2025 an unclear linkage between a correct integral and a correct value was treated as scratch work and cost nothing (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two numbers is the rate in the horizontal direction.
errors.name: Vector components presented without labels or in the wrong order
non_conceptual_causes: the two values were listed in the order in which they were computed
the labels were left off when the answer line was written last
errors.observed_behavior: Two correct numbers appear with no indication of which is the horizontal and which the vertical component.
errors.scoring_consequence: The guideline accepts separate components only when they are labelled, so an unlabelled pair can lose a point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for each component derivative on its own before any quotient is formed.
errors.name: Component derivative computed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the chain rule factor from the inner function was dropped
the wrong component was differentiated
the calculator was in degree mode when the derivative was evaluated
errors.observed_behavior: One of dx/dt or dy/dt is wrong, so every later quantity built from it is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point that depends on that component is lost, though a declared incorrect component may be imported into later parts without further loss (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical answer presented with no setup
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for a vector component, a length, an area, or a derivative with no supporting expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: An unsupported correct acceleration vector earned one of two points in 2023, and an unsupported distance earned neither of two (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what units the reported number carries and compare them with the units a rate would carry for this quantity.
errors.name: Difference reported without the quotient
non_conceptual_causes: the denominator is left for the last line and the work stops before it
the two inputs are equal in the misread stem, so no division seems needed
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the change in the function values over the interval without dividing by the change in the inputs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point requires both a difference and a quotient using values from the table, so a difference alone does not earn it (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two inputs the question names and have the student point to those rows before computing.
errors.name: Rows used that do not match the requested interval
non_conceptual_causes: an adjacent pair of rows is used because the named rows are further apart in the table
the interval endpoints in the stem are read from the wrong column
errors.observed_behavior: The response estimates the derivative from a pair of tabulated inputs other than the pair the question names or the pair that brackets the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the supporting work does not use the values the question specifies.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity was divided by what in the computation, and what unit that division produces.
errors.name: Units omitted or given as the units of the quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the units are copied from the table header, which records the quantity rather than its rate
the units are written on scratch work and not transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports an estimated derivative with no units, or with the units of the modelled quantity rather than of its rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is lost; it is earned for the correct compound units whether or not they are attached to a value, and an equivalent compound form is accepted (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two table entries were used and what was done with them: an answer that the quotient alone is the object is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, an answer that the tabulated amounts are already the rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming both entries at once is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Difference quotient presented without the difference
non_conceptual_causes: the subtraction and division are done on the calculator and only the result is written
the two table entries are differenced mentally
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is written as a single quotient or as a bare number with no visible difference of tabulated values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 rubric states that the setup expression by itself is not sufficient for the point, which requires the answer together with a difference and a quotient using values from the table (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which conditions the theorem requires before the conclusion may be drawn.
errors.name: Theorem hypotheses not stated before the conclusion is used
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
misread of the question or the figure
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the Mean Value Theorem or the Extreme Value Theorem and never mentions continuity or differentiability on the stated interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost even when the conclusion is correct, because the guideline makes the continuity statement a condition of that point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the function is continuous on the closed interval: an answer that the theorem's name is enough is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, an answer that the conclusion may be used regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, and a correct spoken answer with the sentence missing only on paper is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Continuity not drawn from the given differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: the continuity sentence is written on scratch work and never transferred to the response
the stem's phrase differentiable on the closed interval is skimmed and read as already continuous
the part is reached late and the hypothesis sentence is the first thing cut
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that the function is continuous without saying that differentiability supplies it, or omits continuity altogether.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point tied to the hypothesis is lost; the 2025 guideline refused a bare statement that the function is continuous.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the quotient written symbolically before any numbers are substituted: averaging the two endpoint values is consistent with BC-MIS-05003, an integral divided by the interval length is consistent with BC-MIS-99006, and a correct symbolic form carrying a wrong number is consistent with the column and keying causes.
errors.name: Average rate of change formed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the two endpoint values are read from the wrong table columns
the subtraction is keyed into the calculator in the reversed order
the denominator is taken as one endpoint rather than the difference of the endpoints
errors.observed_behavior: The response averages the two endpoint values, reverses the order of subtraction, or divides by the wrong difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the average rate of change is lost and any solved value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which hypotheses the named theorem requires and where each is established here; a student who says the question would not ask unless they held holds the belief, while one who recites them and points at unquoted values omitted the citation.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Many responses failed to explain why r prime was continuous, or discussed the continuity of r rather than r prime, and failed to bound negative 6.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Many responses claimed f is continuous with no justification, and some invoked the Intermediate Value Theorem or the Extreme Value Theorem instead.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: The most common mistake was applying L'Hospital's Rule without first checking that both limits were zero.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Responses stated R is continuous without justification, did not show 155 lies between listed values, or applied the Mean Value Theorem instead.

errors.name: Hypotheses of a theorem not verified before its conclusion is used
non_conceptual_causes: the theorem recalled as its conclusion with the hypotheses left unwritten
the table or graph values that bound the target never quoted
continuity of the derivative confused with continuity of the function when the sentence was written
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses apply the Mean Value Theorem, the Intermediate Value Theorem or L'Hospital's Rule without establishing continuity from differentiability, without bounding the target value between two function values, or without confirming the indeterminate form.
errors.scoring_consequence: The condition point is not earned; in several years this was the point earned by the smallest proportion of responses on the question.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise focusing on stating and checking the hypotheses of each existence theorem, and distinguishing the Mean Value Theorem, the Intermediate Value Theorem and the Extreme Value Theorem by their conditions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what changes in the sentence when the leading fraction is removed.
errors.name: Average value expression interpreted as a total
non_conceptual_causes: read past the leading fraction in the displayed expression
interpreted the expression from the previous part, which was a plain integral
