errors.observed_behavior: A displayed average value expression is described as the total amount accumulated over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is not earned because the description must say average over the interval (sg-24:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the limits were different.
errors.name: Interpretation names the quantity but not the interval
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence was written before the limits were substituted and never revised
the interval was stated in an earlier part and treated as already said
errors.observed_behavior: The sentence says what is accumulating without saying between which inputs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost because the guideline requires the interval as well as the quantity (sg-23:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the expression carries the variable, the base or the exponent.
errors.name: Exponential differentiated by the power rule
non_conceptual_causes: the expression looks like a power because the variable sits in the exponent position
the base and the exponent are exchanged while the term is copied
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the natural exponential as a power of the variable and reduces its exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the curve implied by their own sign statement: classifying from the derivative's value rather than its change is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, expecting the second derivative test to settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, and a sketch that contradicts the written answer is consistent with the reading direction and transposition causes.
errors.name: Direction of the sign change reversed in the classification
non_conceptual_causes: the sign chart is read right to left
the plus and minus labels are transposed when the chart is copied
the classification is carried over from a second derivative test done in an earlier part
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum where the derivative changes from negative to positive, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the plotted curve and the function under discussion separately before answering: treating the drawn curve as the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, treating the derivative as fixing the function outright is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, and labelling both correctly on request is consistent with the axis label and transcription causes.
errors.name: Plotted derivative read as the function itself
non_conceptual_causes: the axis label on the figure is not read
the figure is carried over from a previous part where the function itself was plotted
the curve is labelled correctly on scratch work and the answer sentence names the wrong object
errors.observed_behavior: The response answers a question about the function by describing features of the curve shown, which is the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every part that rests on the plotted object is answered about the wrong function.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative immediately on each side: an answer that every critical point is an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, a classification drawn from the size of the derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and reporting the same sign twice once asked is consistent with the test point and multiplicity causes.
errors.name: Critical point with no sign change declared an extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the sign of the derivative is tested on one side of the input only
the test point chosen on one side lies beyond the next critical point
a factor of even multiplicity is charted as a sign change
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum or minimum at an input where the derivative is zero but keeps its sign on both sides.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the function value at each end of the interval: an answer that only critical points are candidates is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, an answer that a local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and computing the endpoints readily is consistent with the timing and misreading causes.
errors.name: One or both endpoints omitted from the candidate comparison
non_conceptual_causes: the candidate table is begun with the interior points and the part ends before the ends are reached
the interval is read as open
the endpoint value needs a further integral that is left uncomputed
errors.observed_behavior: The response compares values only at the interior critical points and never evaluates at the ends of the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the 2023 guideline states that a response not considering both endpoints does not earn it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether any other input could give a larger value: an answer that a local high point is the highest is consistent with BC-MIS-05007, an answer that the local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and completing the comparison on request is consistent with the endpoint and timing causes.
errors.name: Relative extremum reported as the absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoint values are never evaluated
the word absolute in the stem is skimmed
the comparison table is begun and abandoned when the part runs out of time
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds a local high or low point and reports it as the largest or smallest value on the interval without comparing the rest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is local where a global claim was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Recompute one disputed entry and compare with the table: a candidate list that was never questioned is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, reporting the last entry computed is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, and a corrected entry with the method intact is consistent with the sign and row causes.
errors.name: Function evaluated incorrectly at a candidate
non_conceptual_causes: a sign is dropped while substituting a negative input
the area of one region under the graph is counted without its sign
the accumulated value is taken from the wrong row of the table
errors.observed_behavior: One entry of the candidate table is wrong, whether by substitution or by an area computation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline withholds it for any evaluation error at a candidate.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a curve that is decreasing and concave up at once: an answer that no such curve exists is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, an answer that the second derivative behaves like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and drawing it correctly while the written answer still swaps the two is consistent with the referent and ordering causes.
errors.name: Increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the word increasing in the stem is attached to the plotted curve rather than to the function
the sign chart is built from the plotted curve's values instead of its slopes
the two questions inside the part are answered in the reverse order
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concavity where monotonicity was asked for, or reports increase of the function where the derivative graph is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported belong to the other question and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the plotted curve is rising or falling on the disputed stretch: conflating concavity with monotonicity is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, taking the plotted curve to be the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, and answering rising correctly while the written work used positive is consistent with the carry-over and wording causes.
errors.name: Concavity read from the sign of the plotted derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the chart is built from where the plotted curve lies above the axis because that is what an earlier part needed
the figure's axis label is not read
the words rising and positive are used interchangeably in the answer sentence
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concave up where the plotted derivative is above the axis rather than where it is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported are those of increase, so both the interval point and the reason point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the input between the two stretches: merging them anyway is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, arguing from the function's own sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, and separating them on request is consistent with the transcription and window causes.
errors.name: Interval of increase reported across a gap in the domain
non_conceptual_causes: the two intervals are merged when the answer is copied from the sign chart
the undefined input lies outside the calculator window that was used
the union symbol is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The response merges two intervals of increase into one although the function is undefined between them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval reported is wrong and the reason point falls with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope on each side of the point separately and then ask whether the two agree.
errors.name: Slope read at a point where a graph is not differentiable
non_conceptual_causes: the corner sits close to a grid line, so a nearby straight segment is read as the tangent
the one sided slopes are computed but only the right hand one is reported
errors.observed_behavior: A slope is reported at a corner or a cusp of a supplied graph as though the derivative existed there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is wrong, and the response misses that the correct answer is that the derivative does not exist.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label each substituted number with the symbol it stands for before the rule is applied.
errors.name: Function value used where a derivative value was required
non_conceptual_causes: the function column and the derivative column of the table are adjacent and the wrong one is read
the four required values are copied in one pass and two of them are swapped
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the value of a function into a position in the product or quotient rule that calls for the value of its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the numerator limit and the denominator limit as two separate statements: an answer that the form is itself a value is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, an answer that infinity is available for arithmetic is consistent with BC-MIS-99008, and separating the two limits on request is consistent with the shorthand and equals sign causes.
errors.name: Quotient written explicitly equal to an indeterminate form
non_conceptual_causes: the shorthand is carried over from scratch work
the two limits are evaluated mentally and only the quotient is written
the equals sign is used to link the steps rather than to assert equality
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the limit of the quotient equal to zero over zero rather than presenting the two limits separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2023 rubric states that a response presenting a limit explicitly equal to zero over zero does not earn the first point, and the Chief Reader report names this arithmetic with infinity (sg-23:14, cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would have to be true for the rule to be usable here: an answer that it serves any awkward limit is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, an answer that the indeterminate form is a number is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, and stating the condition correctly with none written is consistent with the mental check and timing causes.
errors.name: Rule applied with no verification of the form
non_conceptual_causes: the verification is done mentally and never written
the rule is applied because the expression is a quotient
the verification sentence is cut when the part is written at speed
errors.observed_behavior: The derivatives of numerator and denominator are taken with no statement that the limit was indeterminate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost; the CED unit overview states that students must show that the rule applies, and BC-ERR-99008 records unverified hypotheses across years (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the symbol written on the right of the equals sign names a number, and if not, what the line is asserting.
errors.name: Limit written as equal to zero over zero
non_conceptual_causes: the shorthand used on a class board is carried into the written line
the equals sign is used as a separator between steps rather than as a claim of equality
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the limit explicitly set equal to the symbol zero over zero rather than presenting the limits of numerator and denominator separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for establishing the form is not earned by a limit presented as equal to zero over zero; two separate limits are required (sg-23:14).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how long each of the stated number of equal steps is.
errors.name: Step size taken as the whole interval
non_conceptual_causes: read the number of steps as the number of points in the table
divided the interval correctly on scratch paper and used the undivided length in the computation
errors.observed_behavior: The response uses the full distance to the target input as one step although several equal steps were asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost because the step size is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the slope is evaluated at on the first step.
errors.name: First Euler step taken with the wrong initial values
non_conceptual_causes: took the initial values from the previous part rather than from this stem
substituted the target input into the derivative by reading the wrong column of the working table
errors.observed_behavior: The first step starts from a point other than the given initial condition, or evaluates the derivative at the target input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost; the 2025 guideline names the correct initial condition as one of its three conditions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both the input and the output used at the start of the second step.
errors.name: Second Euler step restarted from the initial value
non_conceptual_causes: reused the first slope because it was the value already written down
carried the new input forward and the old output, so only half the point was updated
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the derivative again at the initial point instead of at the approximation the first step produced.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost in the 2024 shape, where two correct steps are required.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the columns of their own working and reproduce the intermediate point.
errors.name: Approximation reported with no visible steps
non_conceptual_causes: did the steps on the calculator and recorded only the final display
wrote the table on scratch paper and copied across the answer alone
errors.observed_behavior: A single number appears with no expressions and no labelled table.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost, and an unlabelled table with a wrong answer earns nothing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happened to the differential on the untouched side.
errors.name: Only one side antidifferentiated
non_conceptual_causes: treated the side holding only the differential as already finished
integrated both sides in the working and copied one result across
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the dependent side and leaves the independent side untouched, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The antiderivative point is lost and every later point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the dependent variable at a stated input.
errors.name: Answer left implicit when an expression was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: stopped at the implicit line when the part was the last one attempted
read the command verb as find a relation rather than as express the dependent variable
errors.observed_behavior: The response stops at an equation relating the two variables rather than solving for the dependent one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final solving point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second term becomes when the substitution is written with parentheses; a student who then corrects the whole expansion lost parentheses, while one who also relocates the centre holds a belief about what substitution does.
errors.name: Substitution into a known series carried out incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the substituted expression not enclosed in parentheses before being raised to the power
a constant factor applied to the first term only
the substitution made in the displayed terms and not in the general term
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99009.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes an expression for the variable in a known series but does not raise the whole expression to the required power, or loses a constant factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The resulting series is wrong from the first affected term onward.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask only for the three subinterval widths from the same table; correct widths with a wrong sum points away from BC-MIS-06001.
errors.name: Uniform width applied to a nonuniform partition
non_conceptual_causes: read the first two table inputs, saw one gap, and reused it for the rest
subtracted consecutive inputs correctly but copied one difference twice
reused the layout of a previous uniform partition problem without rereading the inputs
errors.observed_behavior: The response multiplies every tabulated value by one common width although the table inputs are unevenly spaced.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form point is lost because more than one of the six factors is incorrect, and the answer point is lost with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of one term of the sum; rate units alone indicate BC-MIS-06001 rather than a transcription loss.
errors.name: Riemann sum reported as a sum of function values
non_conceptual_causes: copied the table row into the calculator as a list and added it
wrote the widths on scratch paper and never transferred them into the displayed expression
errors.observed_behavior: The response adds the tabulated rate values without multiplying each by a subinterval width.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the form point nor the answer point is earned because no products appear.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the left sum and the right sum on the same table and see whether the student can produce both on request.
errors.name: Endpoint opposite the one requested used in the Riemann sum
non_conceptual_causes: read past the word left or right in the stem
started the sum at the first table row out of habit and never checked which endpoints that uses
errors.observed_behavior: A completely correct Riemann sum is built with left endpoints when right endpoints were requested, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: A completely correct sum of the wrong type earns one of the two remaining points in 2023 and the form point only in 2025 (sg-23:3, sg-25:13).

errors.discriminating_probe: Supply a rate that decreases on part of the interval and increases on the rest and ask whether a direction can be decided at all.
errors.name: Over or under estimate claimed without reference to the behaviour of the function
non_conceptual_causes: stopped writing after the numerical answer when the part was the last one attempted
stated the direction from a remembered table of cases without rereading the given behaviour
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that an approximation is an underestimate or an overestimate but cites no monotonicity or concavity evidence.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is not earned even when the direction stated is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw one rectangle over an increasing arc and say whether it sits above or below the curve.
errors.name: Under and over estimate directions interchanged for a monotone integrand
non_conceptual_causes: recalled the memorised pairing of left with under and stated its opposite
read the graph as decreasing because the axis scale runs downward
errors.observed_behavior: A left sum is called an overestimate for an increasing function, or a right sum an underestimate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost and the answer point with it when the direction is part of the answer.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand a short product first, differentiate the expansion, and compare with the reported answer.
errors.name: Product differentiated as a product of derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: the sum rule pattern from the preceding line is carried into the product
only one of the two product rule terms is transcribed from the scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: The response multiplies the derivatives of the two factors together.
errors.scoring_consequence: The rule point and the result point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the integrand at one input and compare it with a hand estimate; agreement rules the mode setting out.
errors.name: Calculator left in degree mode for a trigonometric integrand
non_conceptual_causes: calculator left in degree mode from earlier use and never reset
mode changed by a memory reset or a borrowed calculator and not checked before the first evaluation
the trigonometric value was entered in a second calculator window whose mode differs from the first
errors.observed_behavior: Numerical values of an integral or of a rate involving a trigonometric function are computed in degree mode.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point that the value would otherwise earn is not earned, and the response remains eligible for subsequent points (sg-23:4).
errors.single_cause_note: No internal misconception is plausible here, since the same student produces correct radian work by hand; the behaviour is a tool state, so the alternatives below are all non conceptual.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to recompute the speed at one time directly from the components.
errors.name: Incorrect speed expression carried into the distance integral
non_conceptual_causes: the speed expression from the earlier part was copied without being rechecked
a component was transcribed into the radical with the wrong sign
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand for total distance is an incorrect speed declared in an earlier part.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integral point is earned and the answer point is not (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both quantities on a path that returns to its starting point.
errors.name: Magnitude of the displacement reported as the distance travelled
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the prompt
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the velocity components, then takes the magnitude, and calls the result the distance travelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand is not the speed (sg-24:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the coordinate at each endpoint has been compared with the value at the candidate.
errors.name: Local argument offered for a farthest point
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that a point on the curve is farthest from an axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:9).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same coordinate with a different starting position.
errors.name: Initial position not added to the accumulated change
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
misread of the prompt
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral of a velocity component is reported as the coordinate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the two u limits explicitly before the antiderivative is evaluated.
errors.name: Original limits of integration kept after a substitution
non_conceptual_causes: converted the limits on scratch paper and substituted from the printed stem instead
wrote the antiderivative in u and stopped before the back substitution when time ran short
errors.observed_behavior: The antiderivative is written in the substituted variable and the original x limits are substituted into it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response is not eligible for the answer point even when the numerical value is correct (sg-23:17, sg-23:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the reported antiderivative and compare it with the integrand.
errors.name: Constant factor from the differential dropped
non_conceptual_causes: solved du for dx correctly and then dropped the reciprocal while recopying
took the inner derivative to be one because the inner expression is linear
errors.observed_behavior: The substitution is carried out without the reciprocal constant that du introduces.
errors.scoring_consequence: The antiderivative point is lost and the value point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the statement by evaluating both sides.
errors.name: Area asserted to equal an expression that is its negative
non_conceptual_causes: the reversed difference was written first and the sign was corrected only in the final value
the expression was transcribed from scratch work in which the order was right
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the reversed difference, sets it equal to the positive area, and reports the positive value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for the incorrect statement even though the reported number is right (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what equation produced the listed inputs: an answer that any listed input is automatically an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the list is itself the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and reciting the equation immediately is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Zeros of the derivative listed without stating the derivative condition
non_conceptual_causes: the equation is solved on the calculator and only the roots are copied
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
the part is written last and only the answer line is filled
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes down the inputs at which the derivative vanishes but never presents the equation setting the derivative equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point of the candidates test is lost; the 2023 guideline states that listing the zeros is not sufficient.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two computed numbers is a slope and which is a height.
errors.name: Function value used as the slope of the tangent line
non_conceptual_causes: the function value and the derivative value are computed in one pass and the wrong one is placed in the slope position
the point of tangency is written first and its second coordinate is reused as the slope
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the tangent line using the value of the function at the point as its slope.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point and the equation point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the noun the question asks for: treating location and value as the same answer is consistent with BC-MIS-05015, reporting whichever candidate was computed last is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, and correcting the answer immediately is consistent with the unlabelled table and transfer causes.
errors.name: Location reported where the value was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: the question's noun is skimmed and the other quantity is reported
the answer is copied from a candidate table whose columns are unlabelled
both quantities are computed and the wrong one is transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response names the input at which the extremum occurs when the question asked for the extreme value, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the 2023 guideline awarded it only for the minimum value, not for the input.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one disc of a stated radius.
errors.name: Radius left unsquared in a solid of revolution integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the integrand was keyed in
the setup was copied from an area between curves exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The disc integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times the square of the function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the area of a circular slice of that radius is.
errors.name: Factor of pi omitted from a solid of revolution integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the factor pi was written outside the integral in scratch work and not carried to the answer line
the constant was left for a final multiplication that time ran out before
errors.observed_behavior: A disc or washer volume is reported without the constant factor pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what feature of the plotted curve makes the claim true; a correct feature named on request points away from BC-MIS-01010.
errors.name: Reason for a feature of the accumulation function phrased only in terms of g
non_conceptual_causes: restated the definition because the justification line was written last and quickly
cited the graph in scratch work and wrote only the conclusion on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: The response says that g has an inflection point because g changes concavity, without tying the claim to the given graph of f.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is earned but the reason point is not, because the reason must be tied to the given graph of f (sg-25:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression whose limit is being taken with its notation; a student who cannot say which variable is limiting holds a notation belief, while one who supplies it at once abbreviated the presentation.
errors.name: Limit taken without limit notation
non_conceptual_causes: the limit symbol dropped when work moved from scratch paper to the answer space
the value written beside the ratio as a running annotation rather than as a statement
the index n left inside the final expression so no limiting variable is identified
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99002.
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the value of a ratio or a quotient as the index grows without writing the limit symbol.
errors.scoring_consequence: Limit notation is required for the setup point in a limit comparison (sg-21:23) and for the limit point in a ratio test (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the two sides of the reported equality are the same object; a student who says the equals sign only marks the next step holds the punctuation belief, while one who separates them and rewrites the line was chaining work.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Strings of equal signs linked expressions that are not equal in the velocity computation.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Responses equated a function with the function evaluated at t equals 4, and equated symbolic second derivatives with numerical values.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: h prime of x set equal to a chain rule expression evaluated at 7, and m of x set equal to 37.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Linkage errors in the speed equation and in the setup for x of 1.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Fourth derivative of f at a general x equated to its value at 0, and g double prime of x equated to g double prime of 0.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: a of t written equal to v prime of t equal to negative 1, mixing a function with a single value.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: h double prime of 6 equated to h double prime of x and to f double prime of x.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: The general speed expression in t equated to the speed at t equals 2.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: h prime of pi equated to an expression still written in x, and two distinct variables used in one equation.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Responses wrote dy in place of dy/dx and dropped the equals zero on the right side after implicit differentiation.

errors.name: Linkage error equating a variable expression with a numerical value
non_conceptual_causes: a calculator result copied onto the end of a symbolic line
several steps of work joined into one chain so that unequal expressions share an equals sign
the value at an instant written over the general expression instead of beside it
errors.observed_behavior: Responses join unequal objects with an equals sign, for example writing a general expression in t equal to the value of that expression at one instant, or stringing several lines of work together with equals signs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The presentation point or the setup point is lost, and in some parts the response becomes ineligible for later points in that part.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise modelling the equals sign as a statement of equality rather than punctuation, never equating a variable expression with a constant, and writing notation such as the derivative evaluated at a point with an explicit subscript or argument.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to derive the formula from the product rule and compare with the line they wrote.
errors.name: Minus sign dropped in the integration by parts expression
non_conceptual_causes: recalled the parts formula with the sign of the product rule instead
wrote the minus on the first line and lost it when the second integral was moved across
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes u times v plus the integral of v du.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression point is not earned, and the answer point depends on it (sg-23:18).
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the response otherwise shows a correct choice of u and dv and the sign is the single departure.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which three properties the integral test requires and where each is checked; a student who names fewer than three holds the belief, while one who names all three but checked them on sample terms has a verification gap.
errors.name: Integral test conditions incomplete or omitted
non_conceptual_causes: one of the three conditions stated and the other two treated as obvious for a familiar function
positivity and decrease checked on the first few terms rather than on the interval
the conditions stated about the terms of the series instead of about the continuous function
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99008.
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the integral test without stating that the function is positive, decreasing, and continuous, or states only one or two of the three.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conditions point requires all three properties to be listed (sg-21:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the first term of the series is and which input produces it; a student who still starts the integral at one holds a fixed starting point, while one who corrects the limit misread the index.
errors.name: Improper integral set up with the wrong lower limit
non_conceptual_causes: the lower index on the sigma read as one out of habit
the integral copied from a worked example that started at one
the first term of the series never evaluated to check which input produces it
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the matching integral from an index other than the one the series starts at.
errors.scoring_consequence: The improper integral point is not earned, although a correct subsequent limit keeps the evaluation point in reach (sg-21:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the improper integral as a limit before any antidifferentiation.
errors.name: Arithmetic with infinity written in place of a limit
non_conceptual_causes: shortcut taken under time pressure
notation habit
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes infinity into the antiderivative rather than taking a limit.
errors.scoring_consequence: The limit notation point is not earned, since limit notation must be used throughout and arithmetic with infinity is disallowed (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which series the comparison was actually performed on; a student who says the two are the same series holds the belief, while one who names the signed series and restates the claim dropped the bars in transcription.
errors.name: Absolute values omitted when absolute convergence is the target
non_conceptual_causes: the word absolutely in the prompt read past
the absolute value bars dropped when the general term was copied into the comparison
the alternating factor cancelled early in the algebra and never restored
errors.observed_behavior: The response runs a comparison or limit comparison on the signed terms while claiming absolute convergence.
errors.scoring_consequence: The explanation point requires absolute value symbols, explicitly or implicitly (sg-21:23).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the limit comparison test licenses when the limit is three; a student who reports divergence from that value holds the criterion confusion, while one who asks for the comparison series' behaviour mixed two adjacent computations.
errors.name: Limit comparison conclusion drawn by comparing the limit with one
non_conceptual_causes: the ratio test and the limit comparison run in adjacent parts and their criteria exchanged
the limit value compared with one because one is the number the previous part used
the comparison series' behaviour never stated, so the only available number was the limit
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the limit of the ratio and then compares that value with one, as in a ratio test, instead of noting that it is positive and finite.
errors.scoring_consequence: Comparing the limit with one does not earn the explanation point (sg-21:23).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the series the conclusion is about; a student who cannot choose between the printed series is conflating them, while one who underlines the right series immediately omitted the referent in writing only.
errors.name: Conclusion states convergence without naming which series it is about
non_conceptual_causes: the pronoun it used because the several series in the part were never labelled
the verdict written in the margin beside one printed series and not repeated in the sentence
the closing sentence compressed after a long test computation
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99001.
errors.observed_behavior: With several series present in one part, the response concludes that the series converges without identifying which one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The explanation point is not earned, because the reader cannot tell which series the claim is about (sg-21:23).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10001 is a plausible internal cause; the rest of the behaviour is a failure to name the subject rather than a belief about series.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how far the interval reaches from its centre; a student who says the interval is the radius holds the conflation, while one who halves the width at once answered the previous part's question.
errors.name: Interval presented where the radius of convergence was requested
non_conceptual_causes: the word radius in the prompt read as interval
the last expression produced by the algebra copied onto the answer line
the half-length never computed because the interval was the object of the previous part
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the inequality and presents an interval without naming the radius as a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The radius point cannot be earned by presenting an interval alone (sg-21:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the first two terms of the series as printed; a student who still uses the index zero term holds the belief, while one who corrects a on sight lost the lower index when reading.
errors.name: First term taken as the index zero term when the series starts elsewhere
non_conceptual_causes: the lower index on the sigma read as zero
the series re-indexed without the compensating factor of r
the first two terms never written out before the formula was applied
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the geometric sum formula with a first term read from the index zero position although the series as written starts at a different index.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported sum is wrong by a factor, so the value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what units the reported number carries and whether they match the units of a rate for the described quantity.
errors.name: Average rate of change reported as a difference
non_conceptual_causes: the division by the change in the input is left for the end and never carried out
the interval endpoints are misread from the stem so the denominator is one
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the change in the function over the interval without dividing by the change in the input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the average rate with supporting work is lost because the quotient is absent.

errors.discriminating_probe: Show both expressions side by side and ask for the units of each.
errors.name: Average value computed where an average rate of change was asked, or the reverse
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the prompt
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response builds a difference quotient when the average of the function values was requested, or an integral quotient when the average rate of change was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned, because the quantity is not the one asked for (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line they wrote: an answer that the tangent line is the function near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that treats the equals sign as punctuation between steps is consistent with BC-MIS-99011, and a correction on substitution is consistent with the transposition and recall causes.
errors.name: Tangent line written with the point and the slope exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the point coordinates are transposed when copied
the slope from the previous part is substituted into a coordinate slot
the point slope form is written from memory with the terms in the wrong places
errors.observed_behavior: The point-slope form is assembled incorrectly, so the coordinates appear where the slope belongs or the line does not pass through the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost; the 2025 report records multiple sign and parenthesis errors arising while isolating the dependent variable, which was not required (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the tangent line touches before the substitution is made: an answer that the line stands in for the function anywhere is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a single coordinate names the point is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, and naming the correct point at once is consistent with the row and reuse causes.
errors.name: Supplied derivative evaluated at the wrong point
non_conceptual_causes: the coordinates are read from the wrong row of the table
the point from an earlier part of the question is reused
only one coordinate is substituted into an expression needing both
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the derivative involving both coordinates is evaluated at coordinates other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost, though the approximation point may still be earned on the incorrect slope (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which input the question asks about and which the tangent line was built at: an answer that the line and the function agree near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a value and a rate are the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming the two inputs correctly is consistent with the misreading and skipped step causes.
errors.name: Tangent line evaluated at the point of tangency
non_conceptual_causes: the nearby input in the stem is misread
the tangent line is written and the substitution step is skipped
the function value already computed is reported because it is on the page
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is produced by substituting the point of tangency rather than the nearby input, so the function value at the known point is returned.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors in the coordinate before differentiating.
errors.name: Product rule omitted when differentiating r times a trigonometric factor
non_conceptual_causes: one of the two factors was dropped while the derivative was written
the derivative was copied from scratch work in which only one factor had been differentiated
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of a Cartesian coordinate in polar form is taken as the product of the two derivatives or of one derivative alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative and everything built from it are wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative expression before the value.
errors.name: Polar derivative value given with no sign of differentiation
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative was taken on the calculator and only the decimal was copied
the expression was written in scratch work and never transferred
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal for dr/dtheta appears with nothing showing that r was differentiated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the response to indicate differentiation of r (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity r measures before the derivative is interpreted.
errors.name: Rate of change of r described as the speed of the particle
non_conceptual_causes: the word rate in the stem was read as speed
the sentence was copied from a particle motion part of the same question
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation of dr/dtheta names the speed along the curve rather than the rate at which the distance from the origin changes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation is wrong, and the chain rule part built on it reports the wrong quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the introduced symbol stands for in terms of the functions in the stem; a student who answers at once omitted the definition, while one who cannot say is treating the symbols themselves as the argument.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: Many responses created a variable s, wrote the area as its square and differentiated, but never stated that s is the difference of the two given functions.

instances.question: Q2
instances.summary: The report states that many students introduced variables without clearly defining them, which made it difficult for them to see the connection to the given functions.

errors.name: Variable introduced without being defined
non_conceptual_causes: a general formula recalled in its own letters and used verbatim
the substitution back to the functions given in the stem left unwritten
no habit of defining a symbol where it first appears
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses invent a symbol for an intermediate quantity, differentiate with it, and never state what it stands for, so the connection between the new symbol and the functions given in the stem cannot be read.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for expressing the quantity as a function of the given variable is not earned, and the chain rule step that depends on it is unreachable.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-05022 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are omissions in writing the setup rather than beliefs about the mathematics.
errors.teacher_advice: The report advises modelling the definition of every variable at the point where it is first used, and using composition of functions to model a quantity as a function of time (cr-22:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the units of the requested rate are.
errors.name: Rate of the angle omitted from a chain rule product
non_conceptual_causes: the rate of the angle given in the stem was not carried into the product
the product was set up and one factor was lost in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The rate at which the distance from the origin changes with time is reported as dr/dtheta alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The chain rule point is lost (sg-25:10).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to apply the rule to a quotient whose value is known and check the sign of the result.
errors.name: Quotient rule numerator terms reversed
non_conceptual_causes: the two numerator terms are written in the order the factors appear in the expression
the subtraction sign is placed after the terms are written and lands between the wrong pair
errors.observed_behavior: The response subtracts in the opposite order in the numerator of the quotient rule.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost because the derivative carries the wrong sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the inner function as a separate question first, then ask which row of the table the outer derivative should be read from.
errors.name: Outer derivative read at the input rather than at the inner output
non_conceptual_causes: the row of the table at the stated input is read instead of the row at the inner output
the axis label of the supplied graph is read for the wrong function
the inner value is computed correctly but the wrong row is then copied
errors.observed_behavior: In a table or graph based composite, the derivative of the outer function is read at the stated input instead of at the value the inner function produces.
errors.scoring_consequence: The numerical answer is wrong even though the chain rule structure was written correctly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write which function the stem supplied before differentiating: treating position, velocity, and acceleration as unrelated formulas is consistent with BC-MIS-04004, treating a quantity and its rate as the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and identifying the supplied function correctly is consistent with the carry-over and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation performed the wrong number of times for the quantity requested
non_conceptual_causes: the function the stem supplied is not identified before differentiating
the previous part's answer is carried forward as the starting function
the derivative is taken twice out of habit from a practised example
errors.observed_behavior: Acceleration is reported where velocity was asked for, or position where velocity was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although each differentiation performed is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the two attained values and the target value in increasing order.
errors.name: Straddling inequality omitted or reversed
non_conceptual_causes: the two straddling values are read from table rows that do not bracket the target
the comparison of the two endpoint values is made mentally and the inequality is written from memory
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the theorem without displaying the two attained values that lie on either side of the target, or places the target outside them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion point is lost because the hypothesis on the target value is not established (sg-25:12).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask on what grounds the function is continuous on the interval, and whether the stem states that or the family of the function gives it.
errors.name: Continuity asserted without a reason in an existence argument
non_conceptual_causes: the continuity clause is written last and is abbreviated when the time runs out
the hypothesis is treated as supplied by the stem and is not restated in the argument
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the function is continuous but gives no basis for the statement.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the continuity hypothesis is not earned by a bare statement that the function is continuous; the response must say that it is continuous because it is differentiable or give an equivalent reason (sg-25:12).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the named theorem concludes, and compare that conclusion with the one the argument actually reaches.
errors.name: Wrong existence theorem named
non_conceptual_causes: the theorem name is recalled from an adjacent exercise about derivatives
the name is written first and the argument is then built to fit it
errors.observed_behavior: The response names a theorem other than the Intermediate Value Theorem while giving an argument about attained values.
errors.scoring_consequence: A named theorem must be the correct one, so naming the wrong theorem costs the conclusion point although naming no theorem at all does not (sg-25:12).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one trapezoid alone; a correct single trapezoid points to a copying loss rather than BC-MIS-06004.
errors.name: Trapezoidal sum with the factor of one half applied to only one term
non_conceptual_causes: factored one half out front, then reapplied it to the first term as well
dropped the factor while recopying the expression onto the next line
errors.observed_behavior: One or two trapezoid terms are halved and the remaining term is not.
errors.scoring_consequence: At least one of the six factors is incorrect, so the form point may survive but the answer point is lost (sg-25:13).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the width of each subinterval and for the height used on each; a student who reports a common width that the table does not give misread the partition, while one who lists the widths and still omits them from the sum holds the belief that the sum is of the listed values.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Some responses assumed each rectangle had width 3, and many made errors in simplifying the sum; some reported a positive value despite computing a negative one.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: A few responses provided a left Riemann sum where a right Riemann sum was asked.

instances.question: Q1
instances.summary: Setups such as a bare sum of three values, a right Riemann sum, and a common width of 3 for unequal subintervals.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Some responses used a trapezoid formula built on differences of the function values rather than sums, and one copy error in the sum cost the answer point.

errors.name: Riemann or trapezoidal sum setup insufficient or malformed
non_conceptual_causes: the subinterval widths read as uniform from an evenly printed table
the products collapsed mentally and never written down
the trapezoid formula recalled with a subtraction in place of the average
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses assume a common subinterval width where the table gives unequal ones, present the sum of the values without the widths, use the wrong sum type, or apply an incorrect trapezoid area formula.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point requires the sum of the appropriate products to be visible; the answer point follows it.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise requiring enough work to demonstrate the sum type in use, and connecting the definite integral of a rate to the accumulated quantity in applied contexts.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors of the term before differentiating it: an answer naming one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, an answer that treats one factor as fixed is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and naming both factors with one term still missing on paper is consistent with the substitution and transcription causes.
errors.name: Product rule omitted inside a differentiation with respect to time
non_conceptual_causes: the short term is read as one symbol
one factor is replaced by its instantaneous value before the differentiation
the product rule is applied and one of its two terms is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A term that multiplies two varying quantities is differentiated as though one of them were constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The completely correct differentiation point is lost; BC-ERR-99013 names the missing product rule explicitly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the stated numbers would still be true one second later: an answer that all of them would is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that treats the product of two varying quantities as one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, and a correct answer with the early substitution still on paper is consistent with the simplification and setup causes.
errors.name: Instantaneous values substituted before differentiating
non_conceptual_causes: the substitution is made to simplify the algebra before differentiating
the number is read from the stem as a fixed feature of the configuration
the value and the rate of the same quantity are confused in the setup table
errors.observed_behavior: A dimension that varies with time is replaced by its value at the instant before the equation is differentiated, so its rate never appears.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiated equation is wrong and the answer follows it; the CED sample activity asks students to mark which given information always applies and which applies only at an instant, which is the distinction at stake (ced:86).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the single unknown in the equation and isolate it: an answer that the instantaneous relation is already the result is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that differentiates against the wrong variable is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a prompt isolation is consistent with the timing and transfer causes.
errors.name: Requested rate never isolated
non_conceptual_causes: the algebra is left to the end of the question and not returned to
the differentiated equation is taken as the answer because it contains the requested symbol
the isolation is carried out on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The differentiated equation is correct and the response stops without solving for the unknown rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final scoring point is lost although the differentiation points may be earned (cr-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantities the differentiated equation needs and which of them the stem supplies: an answer that the instant's stated values are all there is is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer built from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, and spotting the gap on request is consistent with the auxiliary computation and one line causes.
errors.name: Missing instantaneous value not computed
non_conceptual_causes: the quantity is assumed given because the stem supplies its rate
the auxiliary computation from the relating equation is never attempted
the substitution is done in one line so the omission is not noticed
errors.observed_behavior: A quantity needed for the substitution is absent from the stem and the response substitutes nothing in its place or invents a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The substitution is incomplete and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate both functions at one interior input and say which is larger.
errors.name: Difference of the boundary functions taken in the wrong order
non_conceptual_causes: the two function labels in the stem were exchanged when the integrand was written
the order was copied from an earlier exercise in which the roles were reversed
a minus sign was dropped while the second function was distributed
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the lower curve minus the upper curve, or the left curve minus the right curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point may survive, since either order earned it in 2023, but a negative value reported as an area loses the answer point (sg-23:16, sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the axis at one interior input.
errors.name: Outer and inner radii of a washer exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the two curve labels were exchanged when the integrand was written
the distances to the axis were compared at an input outside the region
errors.observed_behavior: The nearer curve is used as the outer radius, giving a negative integrand.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative volume is reported and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand both expressions for a specific pair of numbers and compare.
errors.name: Square of a difference used where a difference of squares is needed
non_conceptual_causes: the two radius expressions were subtracted before being squared during transcription
a sign was dropped while the squared binomial was expanded
errors.observed_behavior: A washer integrand is written as the square of the difference of the two radii, or a squared difference is expanded term by term.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost, and the value is wrong by the cross term.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the distance from a point on the curve to the stated line.
errors.name: Radius measured from a coordinate axis when the axis of revolution is elsewhere
non_conceptual_causes: the line of revolution in the stem was read as a coordinate axis
the subtraction was set up on the figure and not carried into the integrand
errors.observed_behavior: The response revolves about a line other than an axis but writes the radius as the bare function value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the length of a straight segment of slope one on an interval of length one should be.
errors.name: Arc length integrand written without the radical or without the added one
non_conceptual_causes: the radical was written in scratch work and the answer line was copied from an earlier step
the formula was recalled from a note in which the added one had been omitted
errors.observed_behavior: The length integral is written as the integral of the derivative, or of the square root of the derivative squared alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the integrand for a linear function and compare with the Pythagorean length.
errors.name: Derivative not squared inside the arc length radical
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the radical was keyed into the calculator
the square was written outside the radical and then cancelled during simplification
the derivative was substituted into a formula copied with the square already removed
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the square root of one plus the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-08024 is a plausible internal cause here, since the structure of the radical is the single idea at issue; the non-conceptual causes carry the alternatives.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the limits of the integral tell about the piece of curve being measured.
errors.name: Arc length identified without naming the interval
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence was written before the limits were substituted and never revised
the interval was named in an earlier part and treated as already said
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the integral gives the length of the curve but does not say on which interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval point is lost while the arc length point stands (sg-24:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the second term divided by the first and the third divided by the second; matching quotients that still differ from the reported r point to a slip, while a student who declines to form the quotients is reading the ratio off the form.
errors.name: Common ratio of a geometric series misidentified
non_conceptual_causes: the base of the power read off as the ratio with no quotient formed
a sign dropped when consecutive terms carrying an alternating factor were divided
the quotient formed from terms of a series that was written out incorrectly first
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99038.
errors.observed_behavior: The response names a ratio that does not equal the quotient of consecutive terms, often taking the coefficient or the exponent as the ratio.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sum and the convergence condition both follow from the ratio, so the part is lost from that step onward.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10003 is a plausible internal cause; the remaining routes to this behaviour are slips in forming the quotient.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of r and whether the formula applies before any sum is computed; a student who states the condition and then still sums holds the belief, while one who states the condition and withdraws the sum skipped a step.
errors.name: Geometric sum formula applied with a ratio of size at least one
non_conceptual_causes: the closed form written from memory before the ratio had been named
the absolute value bars dropped, so a ratio of negative two was read as less than one
the check skipped because the same formula was applied correctly earlier in the question
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the closed form for the sum without checking that the absolute value of the ratio is less than one, and reports a finite value for a divergent series.
errors.scoring_consequence: A finite value reported for a divergent series loses the answer point and any reasoning point attached to it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two inputs bound the region and why.
errors.name: Limits of integration taken from the wrong inputs
non_conceptual_causes: the intersection abscissas were solved for and the ordinates were copied instead
the calculator window settings were used as the endpoints
one of the two intersection values was transcribed with a sign error
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is set up with limits that are not the boundary of the region or the interval requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, and in 2023 incorrect limits also made a response ineligible for the final area point (sg-23:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope should be when the path is a straight line of slope two.
errors.name: Slope written as dx/dt divided by dy/dt
non_conceptual_causes: the numerator and the denominator were exchanged when the quotient was transcribed
the quotient was copied from scratch work written on its side
errors.observed_behavior: The quotient of parametric derivatives is taken in the reciprocal order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that the calculator evaluated.
errors.name: Slope value presented without the quotient
non_conceptual_causes: the quotient was evaluated on the calculator and only the decimal was copied
the expression was written in scratch work and the answer line was filled last
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal appears for the slope with no expression showing dy/dt divided by dx/dt.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the communication of the quotient (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the speed of a particle whose two component rates are three and four.
errors.name: Component rates added instead of combined as a magnitude
non_conceptual_causes: the radical collapsed to a sum when the expression was transcribed
the two rates were keyed in without their squares
errors.observed_behavior: The speed or the arc length integrand is the sum of the two rates rather than the square root of the sum of their squares.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say what the exponent reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost inside a squared component
non_conceptual_causes: a closing parenthesis was omitted when the integrand was keyed in
the exponent was written over only the first factor in the handwritten expression
errors.observed_behavior: A squared component is written so that only part of it is squared.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost while the answer point remains available, and the same error is not assessed again in a later part (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second derivative does on each side of the disputed input: an answer that a zero suffices is consistent with BC-MIS-05021, an answer drawn from monotonicity instead is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and reporting the sign change correctly on request is consistent with the listing and transfer causes.
errors.name: Point of inflection declared with no sign change checked
non_conceptual_causes: every zero of the plotted curve is listed because the part asks for a list
the sign of the second derivative is tested on one side only
the check is made on the figure and the written sentence reports the zeros alone
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports every zero of the second derivative, or every zero of the plotted curve, as a point of inflection.
errors.scoring_consequence: An extra input in the list costs the answer point outright.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which plotted feature makes the second derivative change sign there: restating the conclusion as the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, treating the symbols as completing the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the feature at once is consistent with the template and timing causes.
errors.name: Inflection reason restated in second derivative symbols
non_conceptual_causes: the symbolic sentence is copied from a memorised template
the plotted object is named in an earlier part and treated as still named
the justification is written at the end of the part in the shortest form to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the second derivative changes sign there, without tying the claim to the plotted object the question supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost while the answer point stands; the 2025 guideline names this split directly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to replace every pronoun in the justification with a name; a student who cannot decide between f, f prime and f double prime is arguing about whichever curve is drawn, while one who names the right function at once wrote loosely.

instances.question: Q3

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Ambiguous terms it, the function, the curve, the graph used without saying which of f, f prime, f double prime or the tangent line was meant.

instances.question: Q4

instances.summary: Responses said the function doesn't change signs or it doesn't change signs rather than naming f prime.

instances.question: Q6
instances.summary: Explanations such as plugging y into the equation makes it undefined or the denominator must be 0 left the subject unnamed.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Reasons such as because it is negative or the function is concave down did not identify the function.

instances.question: Q3
instances.summary: Justifications for the relative maximum referred to the slope, the graph of the slope field or the graph of H.

instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Critical point reasons used the graph or the slope, or described f without connecting it to g prime.
