instances.question: Q4
instances.summary: Reasoning tied to g double prime or f prime rather than to the given graph of f, and critical values were not identified as belonging to g.

errors.name: Vague referent in a justification
non_conceptual_causes: the pronoun written because the functions in play were never labelled on the page
the justification composed as a spoken sentence in which the subject was already understood
the referent dropped when a long argument was condensed into its last line
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses justify behaviour with an unnamed subject such as it, the function, the graph or the slope, so the reader cannot tell whether the claim is about f, f prime, f double prime, the tangent line or the quantity being modelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reasoning or justification point is not earned even when the stated conclusion is correct.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise modelling and requiring precise mathematical language, labelling every intermediate result so that a name is available, and describing behaviour of a function or its derivative over an interval rather than at a point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the derivative at one input inside the disputed interval: reading the derivative's sign from the function's sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, reading it from the second derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and a corrected sign on recomputation is consistent with the substitution and test point causes.
errors.name: Sign of the derivative misread on an interval
non_conceptual_causes: a test value is substituted into the function rather than into the derivative
the sign of a negative factor is dropped while multiplying the factors in the chart
the test point falls outside the interval it was meant to represent
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the derivative expression on one of the intervals of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported intervals are wrong, which also forfeits the reason point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many critical points the function has on the interval: an answer that a local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, an answer that a relative extremum is automatically absolute is consistent with BC-MIS-05007, and supplying the uniqueness sentence on request is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Sole critical point claim made without stating uniqueness
non_conceptual_causes: the uniqueness sentence is held in mind and never written
the interval is not scanned for further zeros of the derivative
the justification is written last and cut back to the classification alone
errors.observed_behavior: The response extends a relative extremum to an absolute one without saying that there is only one critical point on the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification is incomplete because the step that makes the local claim global is missing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state the conclusion in one sentence: naming the theorem but not the claim is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, asserting the claim with no theorem is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, and producing both fluently on request is consistent with the transfer and misreading causes.
errors.name: Existence asserted with no affirmative answer or no theorem
non_conceptual_causes: the affirmative sentence is spoken while working and never written
the theorem name is left on scratch work with the arithmetic
the stem is read as a computation because the previous part asked for one
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the needed arithmetic but never says yes and never names a theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the guideline requires an affirmative answer in some form.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknown rates the differentiated equation contains: an answer assembled from the supplied rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that an instantaneous value holds throughout is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and counting two at once is consistent with the unwritten proportion and timing causes.
errors.name: Extra varying quantity never eliminated
non_conceptual_causes: the similar triangles proportion is seen and never written
the second dimension is assumed constant with no sentence saying so
the differentiated equation is left with two unknown rates and the part ends
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation keeps two varying dimensions that the supplied rates cannot support, and the differentiation produces an equation with two unknown rates.
errors.scoring_consequence: The requested rate cannot be isolated, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name u and dv and then to write the identity before substituting; a student who multiplies two antiderivatives holds the distribution belief, while one who states the identity correctly and still adds the second term lost a sign in an unlabelled layout.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Many responses did not label their work, making it hard to locate errors, and many failed to distribute the subtraction.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Responses added instead of subtracted, antidifferentiated a literal f prime incorrectly, or multiplied two antiderivatives together.

instances.question: Q5
instances.summary: Incorrect choices of u and dv, a wrong sign on the cosine antiderivative, missing parentheses, and an omitted constant of integration.

errors.name: Integration by parts executed or bounded incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: a tabular layout used with no labels, so the alternating signs were lost
the limits of integration written on only one of the two pieces
the second factor antidifferentiated incorrectly while the identity itself was right
errors.notes: Skill mapping inferred from the instance summaries against the names in data/skills.json; the block 99 records carry no unit of their own.
errors.observed_behavior: Responses add instead of subtract the second integral, choose u and dv the wrong way round, multiply two antiderivatives together, antidifferentiate the second factor incorrectly, or misplace the limits of integration between the uv term and the remaining integral.
errors.scoring_consequence: The technique point and the evaluation point are separate, so an unlabelled or mis-signed application loses at least one of them.
errors.teacher_advice: The reports advise significant practice with a clear delineation of u and dv, labels on intermediate steps including tabular work, and writing bounds on the uv term and on the remaining integral.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which shape the area formula in the integrand describes.
errors.name: Factor of pi placed in a polygonal cross section integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the integrand was copied from a disc exercise
the shape named in the stem was read as circular
errors.observed_behavior: A square or triangular cross section volume carries a factor of pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand belongs to the wrong volume family.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which endpoints belong to the interval and how the notation shows that; a student whose spoken answer matches the tests but not the brackets has a notation slip, while one who reports both ends alike is treating the two endpoints as a single case.
errors.name: Interval reported with endpoint inclusion that contradicts the endpoint analysis
non_conceptual_causes: a square bracket written beside the infinity symbol
the brackets written before the endpoint tests were finished
the endpoint findings recorded in scratch work and never transferred to the interval
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests the endpoints correctly and then writes an interval whose brackets do not match the findings, or attaches a closed bracket to an unbounded end.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final interval point requires the interval to match the analysis (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two properties of the terms the test requires and where each was checked; a student who offers one property as sufficient holds the collapse, while one who names both and points to scratch work omitted them in presentation.
errors.name: Alternating series test applied without both conditions stated
non_conceptual_causes: one condition written on the page and the other left in scratch work
the decrease checked on the first three terms rather than for every index
the argument abbreviated because the same test was stated in full earlier in the question
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response invokes the alternating series test or its error bound without stating that the terms alternate and decrease in absolute value to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point requires both conditions to be stated (sg-22:21, sg-24:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the next partial sum is and whether the two answers can both be the value of the series.
errors.name: Value of a convergent series reported as a partial sum
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
arithmetic shortcut taken before the pattern is recognised
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99038.
errors.observed_behavior: The response adds the first few terms of the series and presents that total as the value of the infinite series.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost because the reported number is a partial sum rather than the limit.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number would be if the starting amount were doubled.
errors.name: Net change reported as the amount present
non_conceptual_causes: the phrase asking how much is present was read as asking how much it changed
the initial condition appeared in an earlier part and was not carried into this one
errors.observed_behavior: A question asking how much is present at a time is answered with the net change over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost even when the integral is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the written expression gives at the initial input.
errors.name: Accumulation form written without the initial value or the differential
non_conceptual_causes: copied the accumulation template without the leading term
wrote the differential on the first line and lost it when the expression was rewritten
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the particular solution as an integral alone, or omits the differential from it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression does not satisfy the initial condition, and a missing differential is a notation loss the Chief Reader records name.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say which terms the minus sign reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost when a supplied expression is placed in an integrand
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A subtracted rate or a difference is substituted without parentheses, so only its first term is affected by the operation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is wrong, so the setup point is lost; the Chief Reader records this behaviour across questions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two times the position is known at.
errors.name: Accumulation run in the wrong direction in time
non_conceptual_causes: the limits were written in the order in which the times appear in the stem
a minus sign was dropped when the accumulation was added to the known position
errors.observed_behavior: The integral between the known time and the requested time is added when it should be subtracted, or its limits are in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the guideline lists several correct arrangements of the subtraction and the limits (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the tangent line at a parameter value where dx/dt is zero.
errors.name: Condition that dx/dt is not zero omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the condition was stated in an earlier part and treated as already said
the response ran out of time after the value was found
errors.observed_behavior: The slope formula is applied at a parameter value where dx/dt vanishes, or the condition is never mentioned where the question asks for it.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point that requires the hypothesis is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the equation that the solver was given.
errors.name: Time reported with no speed equation
non_conceptual_causes: the equation was entered in the solver and only the root was copied
the speed expression was written in an earlier part and not repeated
errors.observed_behavior: A time at which the speed takes a value is given with no equation and no speed expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned; the words speed equals the value alone also fail to earn the setup point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the starting and ending inputs and the units of one term before rewriting the sentence.
errors.name: Interpretation of a definite integral omits the interval or the units
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the sentence in abbreviated form after the numerical work filled the space
took the units from the integrand row of the table rather than from the product
errors.observed_behavior: The response names the accumulated quantity but not the interval over which it accumulates, or gives the units of the rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point requires both the accumulated quantity with units and the interval, so it is not earned (sg-23:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate a squared term from the limit definition and compare the result with the rule.
errors.name: Exponent reduced without multiplying by it
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent is reduced first and the multiplying factor is never written in
the original exponent is copied incorrectly, so the factor that should appear is one
errors.observed_behavior: The response lowers the exponent by one but omits the factor of the original exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the graph of the constant term alone looks like and what its slope is.
errors.name: Constant term differentiated to itself
non_conceptual_causes: the constant term is copied along with the rest of the expression before differentiation begins
the constant sits at the end of a long expression and is transcribed without being processed
errors.observed_behavior: The response carries a constant term unchanged into the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the interval in the prompt before writing the quotient.
errors.name: Average taken over an interval the question did not name
non_conceptual_causes: the interval endpoints in the stem were read as the endpoints of the graph window
the limits were copied from the previous part of the same question
the table column for the stated interval was read one row off
errors.observed_behavior: The limits of the average value integral, or the divisor, come from an interval other than the one the prompt states.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the setup point and the answer point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the coordinates of the point the slope was computed at and compare them with the point named in the stem.
errors.name: Slope evaluated at the wrong lattice point
non_conceptual_causes: counted grid lines from the wrong axis when locating the point
read the coordinates off the neighbouring lattice point because the printed dots sit close together
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the segment slope using coordinates taken from a neighbouring point of the grid.
errors.scoring_consequence: The drawn or matched field is wrong at the points that distinguish the candidates.
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the arithmetic on the chosen point is correct and the departure is the choice of point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the numerical slope at two points where the values differ and compare the two drawn segments.
errors.name: Segments drawn with a uniform tilt
non_conceptual_causes: computed the slopes correctly and drew the segments freehand without matching the steepness
drew the whole field before any slope was computed
errors.observed_behavior: The drawn field uses the same steepness everywhere regardless of the computed slopes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The field carries no information and no solution curve can be read from it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values make the rate zero, then ask where those sit on the printed field.
errors.name: Zero slope locus not identified
non_conceptual_causes: solved the right side equal to zero on scratch paper and did not mark the locus on the figure
took the factor equal to zero for only one of its two roots
errors.observed_behavior: The response never solves the right side equal to zero, so the horizontal segments are missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The equilibrium level is unavailable, which costs the sketch point and the critical point work that follows.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the numerical value of dy/dx at the point as a separate question before the second derivative is requested.
errors.name: First derivative value not substituted into the second derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the first derivative value is computed on scratch work and never substituted into the second derivative expression
the point coordinates are substituted into the second derivative before dy/dx is replaced, so the dy/dx symbol is treated as already numeric
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the second derivative containing dy/dx is evaluated without first computing the value of dy/dx at the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The numerical second derivative is wrong, although the product and chain rule points described in the 2025 scoring guidelines may still be earned (sg-25:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the second derivative at one input inside the disputed interval: treating the second derivative as behaving like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, treating concavity and monotonicity as one property is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and a corrected sign on recomputation is consistent with the substitution and differentiation causes.
errors.name: Sign of the second derivative misread
non_conceptual_causes: a test value is substituted into the first derivative instead of the second
a sign is dropped while differentiating the second time
the test point lies outside the interval it labels
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the second derivative on one interval of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The concavity intervals are wrong and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variables appear on the right side of each candidate equation, then ask what that predicts along a vertical line.
errors.name: Dependence on a variable misread from the field
non_conceptual_causes: compared segments along the wrong line of the grid
read the printed segments as differing because the figure is small and the tilts are close
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims the slope varies along a line on which the printed segments are identical, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The match to a candidate equation is made on a false feature.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative on each side, not its size: classifying by magnitude is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, treating every critical point as an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, and giving the signs correctly once asked is consistent with the calculator table and skipped chart causes.
errors.name: Classification taken from the value of the derivative rather than its change
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative values at the two test points are compared in size rather than in sign
the test points are read from a calculator table showing magnitudes only
the sign chart is skipped because the derivative looks monotone
errors.observed_behavior: The response classifies the critical point by whether the derivative is large or small nearby instead of by its sign change.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason does not express a sign change, so the point is lost even when the classification is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the first derivative at that input: an answer that the second derivative test always decides is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, an answer that the two tests are interchangeable is consistent with BC-MIS-05024, and recognising the input is not critical is consistent with the ordering and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Second derivative test applied where the first derivative is not zero
non_conceptual_causes: the critical points are not computed before the test is applied
the input is taken from the stem's list of times rather than from the derivative's zeros
the second derivative is used because it is what the previous part produced
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the second derivative at an input that is not a critical point and classifies it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion does not follow and the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the left side of the differential equation requires before the candidate is substituted.
errors.name: Candidate substituted without being differentiated
non_conceptual_causes: read verify as check the numbers agree
differentiated on scratch paper and transcribed only the substitution line
errors.observed_behavior: The verification puts the candidate into both sides and never produces its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The check does not test the equation, so the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name two different functions that satisfy the same equation.
errors.name: General solution reported as the only solution
non_conceptual_causes: dropped the constant while recopying the solved form
read the definite article in the stem as a claim that the solution is unique
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the family with its constant as a single function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The distinction the essential knowledge draws between a family and a particular solution is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the right side as a product of two single variable factors.
errors.name: Separation attempted on an equation that does not factor
non_conceptual_causes: matched the equation to a separable example with the same letters
moved a term across and dropped the second term of the sum while recopying
errors.observed_behavior: The response moves terms across as though the right side factored when it is a sum in both variables.
errors.scoring_consequence: The separated form is not equivalent to the equation, so nothing that follows is valid.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which input the curve is being touched, and compare that with the input used in the derivative.
errors.name: Derivative evaluated at the wrong input for a tangent line
non_conceptual_causes: the input named in the stem and the input used in an earlier part of the question differ and the earlier one is reused
a sign is dropped in the coordinate while it is substituted into the derivative
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates correctly but substitutes an input other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost and the equation point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each of average value and average rate of change divides, and by what; a student who gives one answer for both holds the conflation, while one who separates them and still integrates the derivative chose the integrand by availability.

instances.question: Q1
